contents.reason: This pair deliberately treats finite real-valued functions; extended-real proper functions, effective domains, and their arithmetic belong to a fuller convex-analysis or optimization development.

sources.locator: Lectures 2–7 and 12, using the source's topic headings

contents.name: Lecture 3, Convex and affine hulls
contents.reason: Affine and convex hull structure is finite convex geometry of sets, whereas this pair builds only the separation machinery required for real-valued convex functions and subgradients.

contents.name: Lecture 3, Carathéodory's theorem
contents.reason: Carathéodory's dimension bound for convex hull representations is a finite convex-geometry theorem not consumed by the function, semicontinuity, Hessian, or subdifferential results on this pair.

contents.name: Lecture 4, Algebra of relative interiors and closures
contents.reason: The algebra of relative interiors under products, sums, and linear images is a set-valued convex-analysis topic not needed for the ordinary-interior statements planned here.

contents.name: Lecture 5, Recession cones and lineality space
contents.reason: Recession cones and lineality describe asymptotic geometry of unbounded convex sets and belong to optimization theory beyond the local and compact function results of this pair.

contents.name: Lecture 5, Directions of recession of convex functions
contents.reason: Directions of recession concern extended asymptotic behavior and existence on unbounded domains, not the finite-valued local continuity and compact-extremum theory developed here.

contents.name: Lecture 6, Nonemptiness of closed set intersections
Lecture 6, Preservation of closure under linear transformation
contents.reason: Closure of linear images requires additional hypotheses and is not used by any separation, subgradient, semicontinuity, or Hessian proof retained on this pair.

contents.name: Lecture 7, Convex conjugate functions
contents.reason: Fenchel conjugates introduce convex duality and extended-real functions, a separate optimization development not required for the elementary Euclidean subdifferential built here.

contents.name: Lecture 7, Conjugacy theorem
contents.reason: The biconjugacy theorem depends on the extended-real closed proper function framework that this finite real-valued page deliberately does not introduce.

contents.name: Lecture 12, Fenchel inequality
contents.reason: Fenchel's inequality is expressed through convex conjugates, which are not defined on this pair and are not needed for the supporting-hyperplane construction of subgradients.

contents.name: Lecture 12, Sensitivity in constrained optimization
contents.reason: Sensitivity of optimal values to constraints is an optimization application of subgradients, not a prerequisite for their Euclidean definition, existence, or minimum criterion.

contents.name: Lecture 12, Subdifferential calculus
contents.reason: Sum, chain, and marginal-function rules for subdifferentials require qualification conditions and an optimization-calculus layer beyond the elementary single-function theory of this pair.
